audits.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship in the Neonatal Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.standard: Local antimicrobial prescribing guidelines and neonatal sepsis evaluation guideline
audits.setting: Neonatal unit, Cork University Maternity Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline 572 days of antibiotic therapy (DOT)/1,000 patient days.

audits.intervention: Educational interventions to improve guideline compliance and introduction of electronic prescribing.

cycle2.result: DOT/1,000 patient days fell from 572 to 417 by March (significant). Therapy >36 hours in negative sepsis work-ups fell from 82 to 7.5 DOT (P = 0.0004); courses >5 days for culture-negative sepsis fell from 46.5 to 7 DOT (P = 0.0009).

audits.other_findings: 312 neonatal admissions across the study; 35% reduction in sepsis evaluations for indications not recognised in the guideline. Two re-audit periods (December 2016, March 2017).
audits.citation: Mccarthy K, Dempsey E. Antimicrobial Stewardship in the Neonatal Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2017;4(Suppl 1):S267-S267.

audits.title: Antimicrobial stewardship in the neonatal unit reduces antibiotic exposure.

cycle1.result: 572 days of therapy (DOT) per 1000 patient days; courses >36 hours in negative sepsis evaluations 82 DOT; courses >5 days for culture-negative sepsis 46.5 DOT.

audits.intervention: Educational interventions and introduction of electronic prescribing in the neonatal unit.

cycle2.result: 417 DOT per 1000 patient days (27% reduction); courses >36 hours in negative sepsis evaluations 7.5 DOT; courses >5 days for culture-negative sepsis 7 DOT.

audits.other_findings: 312 neonatal admissions in total across the study.
audits.citation: McCarthy KN, Hawke A, Dempsey EM. Antimicrobial stewardship in the neonatal unit reduces antibiotic exposure. Acta Paediatr. 2018;107(10):1716-1721. doi:10.1111/apa.14337. PMID: 29603353.

audits.title: A Collaborative Multicenter QI Initiative to Improve Antibiotic Stewardship in Newborns.
audits.standard: CDC core elements for antibiotic stewardship
audits.setting: 146 NICUs in the Vermont Oxford Network Choosing Antibiotics Wisely collaborative

cycle1.result: Baseline NICUs implementing core elements: leadership 15.4%, accountability 54.5%, drug expertise 61.5%, actions 21.7%, tracking 14.7%, reporting 6.3%, education 32.9%.

audits.intervention: Internet-based national QI collaborative with interactive web sessions, four point-prevalence audits and expert coaching

cycle2.result: Leadership 68.8%, accountability 95%, drug expertise 85.1%, actions 72.3%, tracking 78%, reporting 17.7%, education 87.2%; significant reduction in antibiotic use.

audits.other_findings: Antibiotic use rate defined as the percentage of infants receiving 1 or more antibiotics on audit day; exact figures not given in the abstract.
audits.citation: Dukhovny D, Buus-Frank ME, Edwards EM, Ho T, Morrow KA, Srinivasan A, et al.. A Collaborative Multicenter QI Initiative to Improve Antibiotic Stewardship in Newborns. Pediatrics. 2019;144(6):e20190589. doi:10.1542/peds.2019-0589. PMID: 31676682.

audits.title: Reduction of unnecessary antibiotic days in a level IV neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Local consensus guidelines for antibiotic duration; aim to reduce unnecessary antibiotic days by 20% within 1 year
audits.setting: 39-bed outborn level IV NICU, St Christopher's Hospital for Children, Philadelphia

cycle1.result: Unnecessary antibiotic days 42%; antibiotic stop date compliance 32%.

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary stewardship team, consensus duration guidelines, prospective audit of stop dates and documented justification, and repeated educational sessions.

cycle2.result: Unnecessary antibiotic days 12%; stop date compliance 76%.

audits.other_findings: No antibiotics were reinitiated within 2 weeks (balancing measure).
audits.citation: Vyas DP, Quinones-Cardona V, Gilfillan MA, Young ME, Pough KA, Carey AJ. Reduction of unnecessary antibiotic days in a level IV neonatal intensive care unit. Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol. 2022;2(1):e50. doi:10.1017/ash.2022.33. PMID: 36483355.

audits.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a vancomycin stewardship programme in a level IV neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Recommendations to limit vancomycin to known resistant infections
audits.setting: Level IV neonatal intensive care unit, Gazi University, Ankara

cycle1.result: Vancomycin initiated 166 times; 113 days of therapy per 1000 patient days.

audits.intervention: Education of the NICU team, standardisation of vancomycin therapy, and prospective audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Vancomycin initiated 71 times (57.2% reduction); 45 days of therapy per 1000 patient days (60.2% reduction).

audits.other_findings: No increase in length of stay or mortality.
audits.citation: Tas M, Onal E, Tapisiz A, Bas S, Hirfanoglu IM, Tezer H, et al.. Evaluating the effectiveness of a vancomycin stewardship programme in a level IV neonatal intensive care unit. J Hosp Infect. 2025;158:11-18. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2025.01.009. PMID: 39922500.
